Alex / Sergio —

Attached is a short competitor comp (CSV) and my notes. High-level takeaways and a recommended Redwood entry offer to hit the $60–$110 / 1M target while remaining competitive: 

Competitor snapshot (approx list $/1M for generation-like workloads, comparable models):
- OpenAI (hosted gpt-style endpoints): list ~ $140–$220 / 1M (depends on model & context) — enterprise discounts often reduce this by 20–35% with committed spends.
- Anthropic (Claude-like endpoints): list ~ $120–$200 / 1M — committed pricing similar to OpenAI, slightly more favorable on mid-sized commits.
- Managed open-model hosting (various providers on Llama/RedPajama variants): list ~ $40–$120 / 1M depending on quantization and whether the host includes managed optimization/caching.
- Self-hosted (customer-operated on infra): effective infra + ops cost often maps to $25–$80 / 1M at scale but requires heavy engineering/Ops.

Context & levers:
- Batching + KV caching and a quantized model path can materially reduce per-token execution cost; Redwood can offer a "performance-optimized" vs "cost-optimized" profile.
- Committed volume discounts and minimum monthly commits change the math — e.g., 200M+ commit bands move list prices down 25–40% in the market.

Recommended Redwood offer (to propose):
- Option A (Commit-friendly, midsize): 200M tokens/mo commit -> $95 / 1M tokens (base); includes 12mo audit log retention, VPC option, 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated. Add-ons: private deployment setup fee.
- Option B (Aggressive price to win, multi-year): 250M tokens/mo commit -> $70 / 1M tokens (base) with a 12-month MRR commit; includes optimization tuning and a 2-month onboarding credit.
- Option C (No commit, hosted): $140 / 1M tokens with higher latency SLO and limited logging retention (not acceptable for FinEdge prod).

Why these numbers?
- $95 / 1M sits in middle of FinEdge procurement range and undercuts OpenAI list + typical post-discount.
- $70 / 1M is aggressive but still realistic if we secure a 12mo commit and provide optimization (cache, batching) to reduce execution cost.

Attachments: competitor-comps.csv (simple list price comparisons), redwood-pricing-grid-v1.xlsx (Alex shared earlier).

Next steps:
1) Alex: send Options A/B to Emily and procurement with the value-adds (VPC, logs, onboarding credit on Option B).
2) Sergio: confirm Dedicated setup lead time and minimum commit enforcement for Option B.
3) I’ll draft a 1-pager comparison and bring a short ROI slide that maps estimated monthly spend at their 180M baseline.

Let me know if you want me to price a blended hybrid (mix of Dedicated for heavy nightly batches + hosted for interactive calls).

—Marissa
